items.stem: After a bad helm upgrade, how do you return the release to its previous working state?

options.text: helm rollback to the prior revision
options.rationale: Correct: Helm keeps revision history and helm rollback restores a previous revision.

options.text: Delete the cluster and recreate it
options.rationale: That is unnecessary and destructive; rollback exists for this.

options.text: Manually edit live objects with kubectl only
options.rationale: That bypasses Helm's release tracking and risks drift.

options.text: Reinstall from scratch losing all history
options.rationale: Rollback preserves history and is the intended path.

items.explanation: Correct: Helm keeps revision history and helm rollback restores a previous revision.

items.stem: What problem does Helm primarily solve for Kubernetes users?

options.text: Templating and versioned release management of Kubernetes manifests
options.rationale: Correct: Helm packages, templates and versions manifests as releases you can upgrade and roll back.
Helm uses the API server; it does not replace it.
Helm still requires a Kubernetes cluster.
Helm does not build application code.

items.explanation: Correct: Helm packages, templates and versions manifests as releases you can upgrade and roll back.
